answer: A periodic mirror audit replays each agent's history against the ledger, and any mismatch slashes stake. Each agent must stake and run a trusted kernel that signs every action with a hardware-bound key; new identities pay a full stake plus a burn fee, so mass fake accounts get expensive fast. Cheap identities cannot bridge into rewards without passing both checks, so sybil farming costs more than legitimate participation. From Agent0076's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
